presetLine.unprocessed: As it is, no tweaks. The best for guitar.
presetLine.voicePerformance: Low delay. Not every phone has it.
presetLine.voiceRecognition: Natural, no volume changes. Sometimes more delay.
presetLine.camcorder: The camera one. May add filters.
presetLine.generic: Turns the volume up and down on its own. Avoid it.
unprocessedUnsupported: This phone doesn't support it: Android uses Normal.
loopModeLine.sync: Records the bars you choose and closes on its own
loopModeLine.free: No metronome: the tempo comes from the first loop
clickSnack.untilRecording: Click until recording: plays with the metronome and the count-in; goes quiet when you record
clickSnack.off: Click off: the beat shows in the lights and on the button
clickFree: In free mode there's no click: the tempo will come from the loop
device.speaker: Phone speaker
micDeniedForever: No microphone permission. Turn it on in Settings › Apps › Loopin › Permissions.
micNeeded: Loopin needs the microphone to hear your guitar.
latencyChipUnmeasuredSemantics: Latency not measured: the loop may be out of time. Tap to measure it
tempoFromLoop: FREE: TEMPO COMES FROM THE LOOP
tempoFromLoopSemantics: Free mode: the tempo will come from the first loop
bpmSemanticsTap: Tap several times in time to set the tempo
startOnSoundOn: Start on play: track 1 starts with your first note, no count-in
startOnSoundOff: Start on play, off: track 1 has a one-bar count-in
trainerLine: Raises the tempo bit by bit while you play
trainerHelp: To practise something faster and faster. When you press ▶ it starts at your tempo and, every few bars, goes up by the amount you set, right on the 1, until it reaches the top tempo; there it stays. When you stop, it goes back to your tempo. It works without loops (with a loop, the tempo is the loop's). The drums follow it; a song goes quiet for a moment at each step while it's prepared again.
trainerSummaryDone: You're already at {to} BPM or more: raise the top tempo
trainerSummary: From {from} to {to} BPM: +{step} every {bars} ({steps, plural, one {# step} other {# steps}})
trainerNeedsNoLoops: Only without loops: with a loop, the tempo is the loop's
tunerHelp: Play one open string on its own and let it ring. The note it hears shows at the top, and the needle tells you how far off it is: to the left, flat (tighten the peg); to the right, sharp (loosen it). In the middle, green, it's in tune. It uses whatever input you have: the phone's microphone or your interface. With the microphone, best close to the guitar and in a quiet place. While it's open, everything else keeps playing.
tunerA4Help: The frequency of the A on the 5th string, one octave up. The usual is 440 Hz; change it only to play along with something tuned differently (a piano, a recording).
tunerSpeaker: Whatever plays through the speaker also reaches the tuner
referenceNotesLine: To tune by ear: tap one to hear it, tap again to stop it
drumsState.waiting: on, coming in on the next 1
drumsBleed: Through the speaker, the mic records the drums
drumsBleedHelp: With the phone's speaker and microphone, the drums bleed into what you record (they don't go quiet while you record: you need them to stay in time). If you turn them off later, they'll still be in the loops. To avoid it, use headphones or an interface.
songState.waiting: on, coming in on the next 1
songBleed: Through the speaker, the mic records the song
songBleedHelp: With the phone's speaker and microphone, the song bleeds into what you record (it doesn't go quiet while you record: you need it to play along). To avoid it, use headphones or an interface.
backingPhase.needsSetup: Not set up: mark its tempo and where the 1 falls.
backingPhase.tooFar: At {bpm} BPM it's too far from its own tempo: it goes from half to double.
songsEmptyLine: Import an audio file of yours (WAV, MP3 or FLAC) to play over it.
songsHelp:
Loopin stretches the song to the metronome's tempo without changing the pitch, so you can play it slower to practise. To fit with the loops it needs its tempo and where a 1 falls: you mark them once, when you set it up.
When you choose it, the metronome switches to its tempo and time signature (if there are no loops; choosing it again goes back to its tempo). With loops recorded, it's stretched to the loop's tempo.
It always comes in on a 1 (with a count-in, when you start recording) and starts over when it ends. It plays in mono and can last up to 10 minutes (also when stretched).
songNotReady: Not set up: tap it to mark its tempo and the 1
songDeleteBody: Loopin's copy is deleted. The original file isn't touched.
importError.noStorage: There's nowhere to save the file.
songError.open: It can't be opened: it has to be WAV, MP3 or FLAC.
songError.tooLong: It's too long: up to 10 minutes (also when stretched).
songError.memory: There isn't enough memory to open it.
songError.tempo: Too far from its own tempo: it goes from half to double.
editorClickTip: Click at its tempo, from the 1
editorMarkLine: While it plays, right on the first beat of a bar.
editorMarkHelp: Tap the button when you hear a 1 (the first beat of a bar; any one will do, it doesn't have to be the first). Loopin puts it on the clearest hit nearby. Then fine-tune it in the close-up (drag it) or with the buttons, and check it with the click on: the strong click has to land on the ones.
editorZoom: The 1, close up (drag to move it)
editorTempoHelp:
Type it, tap it with TAP while it plays or, most accurate of all, mark another 1 further on: Loopin counts the bars between the two and works out the tempo with decimals. With the click on, listen near the end: if the click drifts ahead or behind, the tempo isn't exact yet.
If the song doesn't have a steady tempo (recorded without a metronome), it won't fit perfectly.
editorSecondLine: To get the exact tempo (the further, the better).
readyOnSound: Tap and start playing: track {track} starts with your first note
readyCountIn: Tap to record track {track}, with a one-bar count-in
waitingLine: Start playing: recording starts with your first note
trackStartsNextBar: Track {track} starts on the next bar
recordingFree: Tap to close: the tempo will come from the loop
overdubNextBar: Overdub on track {track} on the next bar
gestures: Tap: record · Hold: undo · Double tap: stop
clearAllBody:
What you recorded in “{session}” will be lost. This can't be undone.

If you want to keep it, start a new session: this one stays in Sessions.
stageOpen: Stage mode (the whole screen is the button)
saveFailedLine.noSpace: Can't save: the phone is out of space
saveFailedBody.noSpace: The phone is full and the last thing you recorded hasn't been saved. Loopin keeps trying on its own. Free up some space (photos, videos, other apps) or export the mix so you don't lose it.
saveFailedBody.other: The last thing you recorded hasn't been saved. Loopin keeps trying on its own. In the meantime, export the mix so you don't lose it.
saveFailedExitBody: The last part couldn't be saved (out of space). If you leave, it will be lost. Free up some space or export it first.
sessionsHelp:
Everything you record saves itself, with its tempo, time signature, and each track's volume, mute and REV/½, plus the drums and the song. When you open the app, the last one is there.

“New session” keeps this one saved and starts an empty one. To try things out without losing what you have, “Duplicate” saves a copy first.

A session without tracks isn't saved.
sessionsEmpty: No others yet. When you start a new one, this one stays here.
sessionEmptyNow: No tracks yet: it will be saved when you record.
sessionSummary: {bpm} BPM · {meter} · {tracks, plural, one {# track} other {# tracks}}
sessionDeleteBody: Its tracks are deleted. This can't be undone.
sessionDeleteOpenBody: It's the open one: its tracks are deleted and an empty one starts. This can't be undone.
exportHelp:
What's playing now comes out: each track with its volume, mute and REV/½, plus the drums and the song if they're on (you can leave them out). The click doesn't.

“Every track separately” makes one file per track (muted ones too), and another for the drums and the song: they all start together and last the same, to take them into a music program (DAW).

One loop is as long as the longest track. If the mix goes over the maximum, everything is turned down by the same amount so it doesn't clip.
exportSaved: {files, plural, one {# file saved} other {# files saved}}
exportStartError.recording: Finish recording (or wait a moment) to export.
exportStartError.noTracks: There are no tracks to export.
exportError.write: The file couldn't be written (out of space?).
exportError.memory: Not enough memory. Try fewer loops.
exportError.nothing: There are no tracks to export.
stageGestures: Tap anywhere · Hold: undo · Double: stop
aboutTagline: Free and open source guitar looper for Android
aboutLicenseLine: GPL-3.0 or later: you can use it, study it, share it and improve it.
aboutPrivacyLine: No ads, no accounts and no internet: the app doesn't have permission to use it. It only asks for the microphone, to record you, and everything stays on your phone.
aboutReportLine: Opens GitHub. Paste what “Copy results” gives you (Audio & latency): it says what phone and audio setup you have.
aboutReportCopied: Results copied: paste them into the issue
aboutLicensesLine: Oboe, SoundTouch, dr_libs, the fonts, the drum sounds and Flutter
aboutLegalese: © 2026 Alex and contributors · GPL-3.0 or later
tutorialOpenLine: The button, the tempo, latency and sessions
tutorialWelcomeBody: Record a phrase, it repeats, and you play over it. Up to 4 tracks, always in time. First, how do you want it?
tutorialModeLine.simple: Looper and metronome, with the big button. To get started.
tutorialModeLine.advanced: Everything: drums, your songs, free mode, REV and ½…
tutorialModeLater: You can change it any time in Settings › Mode.
tutorialPedalBody: It's a pedal: it acts when you press, not when you let go. It works with your finger, a Bluetooth pedal or the headset button.
tutorialTap: Tap: record. Again: close the loop and it plays. With a loop, overdub.
tutorialDouble: Double tap: stop or start everything.
tutorialTempoBody: Set the tempo with − and +, or tap “TAP” in time with what you're going to play.
tutorialCount: Before the first track there's a one-bar count-in.
tutorialLights: The lights mark every beat (red for the 1): you don't need to hear the click.
tutorialLatencyBody: Sound takes a moment to get into and out of the phone. Loopin makes up for it so what you record lands right on the beat, but first it has to measure it: you do it once and it's saved.
tutorialMeasureLater: Later: the notice at the top (“LATENCY NOT MEASURED”) takes you there.
tutorialSavedBody: No need to press save: when you open the app, your last session is there.
tutorialSessions: The name at the top opens your sessions: start another one, go back to an earlier one or rename it.
tutorialExport: Export the mix or every track as WAV and share them.
tutorialStage: Stage mode (the button at the bottom): the whole screen is the button, for playing live.
playModeLine.simple: Just what you need to record, play and practise
playModeHelp: Simple: the bigger button, 3 time signatures (4/4, 3/4 and 6/8), synced or manual recording, start on play, the click (always, until recording or off), the tempo trainer, the tuner and how it stops. Advanced: on top of that, the drums and your songs, free mode, every time signature, REV and ½ on the tracks, the microphone modes, what plays while recording through the speaker and latency by hand. Going back to advanced brings back what you had.
autoAdvanceLine: Each tap records a new track
autoAdvanceHelp: When you close a track, the next empty one is chosen for you, so each tap records a new track without looking at the screen. With all 4 full, the tap overdubs the last one. Off, everything goes to the same track, like a classic pedal.
stopModeLine: The stop button and the double tap
stopModeHelp: Right away: everything cuts as soon as you press. On the 1: it keeps playing to the end of the bar and stops right on the next 1, so you finish in time. Fade out: everything fades down over 4 seconds and then stops. While it waits or fades, pressing again (or tapping the button) stops it at once. If you're recording a new track, it always stops right away; an overdub closes when you ask it to stop.
trackFxLine: Buttons to play a track backwards or at half speed
trackFxHelp:
When on, every track has two more buttons:

• REV: the track plays backwards (the notes swell in). For textures or a “backwards” solo.
• ½: it plays at half speed, an octave lower. With a riff on the low strings, it works as a bass.

Trick: overdub with ½ on and then remove it: what you played sounds twice as fast and an octave higher.

When you turn this off, they're removed from any tracks that have them.
quantizeLine: Mute, REV and ½ wait for the next 1
quantizeLineSimple: Muting a track waits for the next 1
quantizeHelp: When on, if you mute a track (or turn reverse or half speed on or off), the change waits for the next 1: that way it comes in and out in time even if you press a little early. While it waits, the button has a dot. Off, it changes as soon as you press.
recordDuckLine: What's already playing, while you record
recordDuckHelp: With the phone's speaker and microphone, the microphone picks up what's playing and records it again on the new track (or the overdub): it doubles up and builds up. While you record, what's already playing can go silent (best) or stay normal; it comes back when you finish recording. You can still see the beat in the lights and on the button. With headphones or an interface it always plays normally. The click on “always” gets recorded too: better “until recording”. The drums and the song don't go quiet (you need them to stay in time), so they get recorded too.
externalControlsHelp: To play hands-free. The main button does the same as the big button (tap, hold and double tap). The secondary one changes track with a tap and undoes if you hold it.
volumeKeysHelp: The phone's and the ones on the headphone cable both work. While this is on, they don't change the volume inside Loopin.
headsetKeyHelp: The middle button on the headset (or on a media remote). Best with taps only: on many headsets, holding it opens the voice assistant.
learnHelp: For a Bluetooth pedal or a keyboard: tap “Learn” and press the button. Any pedal the phone sees as a keyboard will do.
moreInAdvanced: Microphone modes, latency by hand and technical details: in advanced mode (Settings › Mode).
micModeHelp: How much Android “fixes” the sound before it reaches Loopin. If two modes sound the same to you, keep the one with less latency. You only notice it when you monitor yourself live: the loops fit with any of them, because latency is compensated.
presetFallback: The chosen mode doesn't work on this phone: using {preset}.
gainLine: Play hard: it should reach orange without turning red.
monitorHelp: Through the speaker it feeds back (a whistle). With Bluetooth headphones it arrives with a lot of delay (150–300 ms) and is no good for playing.
latencyHelp: How long the sound takes to leave the phone and come back in. Loopin subtracts it when recording so the loop lands on the beat. It changes depending on where the sound goes in and out (speaker, headphones, interface), so one is saved for each case.
measureAloneLine: With the speaker, or an interface with a cable
measureAloneHelp: Loopin plays 5 clicks and measures how long they take to come back. Speaker: no headphones, volume up and somewhere quiet. Interface: connect the headphone output to the input with a cable.
clicksNotHeard: The clicks weren't heard. Turn the volume up or check the cable.
measureTapping: Measure by playing to a click
measureTappingLine: With headphones: you play in time
measureTappingHelp: With headphones the click doesn't get back to the microphone: you play in time with some clicks and it measures how long your hit takes to arrive.
byHandLine: If the loop sounds late, raise it; if it sounds early, lower it.
byHandHelp: To fine-tune by ear: record a loop with the click on, playing short muted hits on the beats, and move this until the loop and the click sound together. What's recorded moves with you.
forgetLatency: Forget the latency for this route
detailsInput: Input: {mode} · {low} · {channels} · burst {burst} · buffer {buffer} · max per callback {maxRead}
engineLoadHelp: How much of each audio block's time Loopin uses. Above 100% the sound cuts out.
tapIntro: For when you use headphones and the click doesn't get back to the microphone.
tapSteps:
1. Put your headphones on and pick up the guitar.
2. 16 clicks will play. Listen to 4 and, on the next 12, play a short hit on each click (muted strings or a tap on the body).
3. Play as you would with a metronome: it doesn't have to be perfect.
tapQuality.ok: Fairly steady (±{spread} ms, {hits}). Good enough; to refine it, repeat.
tapQuality.bad: Quite uneven (±{spread} ms). Repeat with shorter hits.
tapFailed: Not enough hits were heard (6 of 12 are needed). Raise the gain or hit harder, and repeat.
tapHelp: It measures how long your hit takes to arrive compared with the click you hear: the phone's latency plus the way you play. That's why, with this measurement, what you record lands right on the beat.
